title: sizzlr: plans and PRs as two-voice review videos

lines.text: Nobody reads the whole plan. Be honest.
Fair. So let the plan talk instead.
Your coding agent reads the plan and writes a short script: who says what, and what's on screen.
sizzlr turns it into voices, scenes and a video. Locally. No API keys.
lines.say: Sizzler turns it into voices, scenes and a video. Locally. No API keys.

scenes.heading: Inside the build
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  S[Script] --> V[Kokoro voices]
  V --> T[Timeline]
  T --> H[HTML scenes]
  H --> R[HyperFrames]
  R --> M[MP4]

lines.text: Kokoro speaks every line, the timeline follows the speech, and HyperFrames renders the scenes to an MP4.
And how long do I wait?
On four cores, about three times the video's length. The calm default renders almost twice as fast.

items.after: Everything on screen comes from the source
A closed catalogue, with ==never for== rules
items.why: No bar charts for font sizes

items.after: One config file: fonts, colours, voices

lines.text: Every number on screen comes from the source.
Elements come from a fixed catalogue, with rules for when not to use them.
And one config file sets your fonts, colours and voices.

One command installs the skill for Claude Code and Codex. Then you just ask.
